note: Every number the RF work quotes, with the script that reproduces it, the document it appears in, and the check that could make it wrong. Modelled on docs/claims.json: PASS-2 = reproduced by an independent path, PASS-1 = one run with its falsifier satisfied, withdrawn = published then failed and is evidence of the retraction only.

claims.claim: the site ceiling height is 2.58 m and the phone's floor-to-ceiling error is +/- 0.09 m, because three separately measured ceilings agree only to 18 cm while the building's ceilings are identical
evidence: Rob's statement that every ceiling in the house is the same height
claims.falsifier: a tape measurement of any ceiling differing from 2.58 m by more than 0.09 m, or two ceilings in the house measured as different heights

claims.claim: ARCore is the instrument for any distance in metres and step counting is not a measurement: three walks of the same 30 m gave 92, 92 and 62 counts, implying strides of 0.326 and 0.484 m from the same body
evidence: stride calibration 0.326 m and 0.484 m, a 48% disagreement
loop closure 9-25% of path length, median 17.6%
two walls of one room agree to 1 cm (6.05 and 6.05 m)
claims.falsifier: a tape measure agreeing with a step-derived distance better than with the ARCore distance on the same room

claims.claim: at a fixed spot with nothing moving the level varies by 16 dB, and over consecutive samples the power is exponential (std/mean 1.21 against Rayleigh's 1.00)
evidence: the same shape in two rooms
claims.falsifier: a fixed-spot series in a room with the same construction showing a spread under 6 dB, or a Gaussian rather than exponential power distribution

claims.claim: no RF finding below 6 dB is a finding, because that is inside the instrument's own noise against a 16 dB fading floor
evidence: the channel plan refuses every gain under 6 dB
claims.falsifier: a change under 6 dB that reproduces as a level shift on a later scan

claims.claim: moving the venue 2.4 GHz access point from channel 11 to channel 1 removes 24 dB of measured interference, because channel 11 is the busiest channel in the neighbourhood
evidence: 17 spot scans, 33 networks, channel 11 occupied by the strongest non-house network at -33 dBm
claims.falsifier: a post-change scan of the same spots showing the interference on channel 1 above -56 dBm, or no level change where the plan predicted 24 dB

claims.claim: moving the 5 GHz radio from channel 36 to channel 40 or 44 removes 31-34 dB of measured interference
evidence: one channel plan over the same 17 scans
rob-site's independent fleet plan on the same data proposes ch 36 -> ch 40 for 34.0 dB
claims.falsifier: a post-change scan of the same spots showing no level change, or interference on the new channel above the 6 dB action floor

claims.claim: the house's measured level spread is 33 dB, from -28 dBm in the router bedroom to -61 dBm in Alice's office, with a cliff between -36 and -56 mid-house
evidence: 9 of 10 walks agree on the same profile
claims.falsifier: a repeat scan showing Alice's office within 10 dB of the router bedroom

claims.claim: the room is a diffuse cavity: the level distribution across a walk is consistent with Rayleigh fading rather than a single strong path
claims.falsifier: a room with the same construction where the distribution is visibly single-path (a dominant direct ray) in the same measurement

claims.claim: a room's dimensions can be recovered from its mode spectrum to under 2% with half the modes missing and 1 Hz of jitter, when the ceiling is known as a prior
evidence: 1.83% with 50% of modes dropped and 1 Hz jitter
claims.falsifier: recovery failing on a measured room spectrum (not a simulated one) at the same damage
